transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

Hi, yeah, thanks. Um, I guess the main thing that pushed me to come in is that I keep getting up from my workstation during the day. I process insurance claims, and even when I know I’m supposed to just stay put and finish my claim reviews, I just... I keep leaving my desk.
Do you feel anxious or uneasy when you're sitting at your desk?

No, not really. Um... I wouldn't say I feel anxious or nervous. It's not like I'm sitting there worrying about anything or feeling stressed out. I just... I don't know, I just kind of get up. Like I'll be looking at a claim and then suddenly I'm walking to the breakroom or just wandering around the office. I don't feel uneasy, I just... have a hard time staying in the chair.
Do you feel like you have to get up from your desk, like something is driving you to do it?

No, not really. It's not like a physical urge or like I'm restless and just have to move. I don't feel driven to do it at all. 

It's more like... I just sort of drift away from what I'm doing. I'll be in the middle of a file, and then I just kind of end up out of my chair getting water or looking out the window. There's no real push behind it, I just sort of lose track of staying put.
Do you find yourself doing the same things over and over again, like checking something multiple times?

No, I don't think so. I haven't noticed anything like that. I don't really have a habit of checking things over and over again, or repeating actions. I usually just look at a claim once and move on. So, no, I don't really do that.
Do you have trouble paying attention to the details of your work, like making careless mistakes on the claims you're reviewing?

No, I haven't really noticed that. I mean, I guess everyone messes up a little sometimes, but I don't really make careless mistakes on the claims. When I'm actually looking at a file and working on it, I can catch the details just fine. So, no, that hasn't really been an issue for me.
Do you find yourself being overly active or restless when you're not at work?

No, not really. I mean, when I'm not at work, I'm usually pretty low-key. I just kind of hang out at home, watch TV or whatever. I don't feel like I have to be constantly moving or doing things. So, no, I wouldn't say I'm overly active or restless on my own time, either.
Do you think you get up from your desk because you're bored with what you're doing?

No, I wouldn't say it's because I'm bored. It's more just... I don't know, I just get up. I don't really feel like I'm doing it because the work itself is boring, I just find myself walking away from the desk.
Do you feel like getting up from your desk is something you've just gotten used to doing over time?

I don't think so. I haven't really thought about it like a habit I've built up over time. It doesn't feel like something I'm doing just out of routine... I just kind of end up away from my desk without really planning to.
Do you have any habits or behaviors that you repeat over and over, even when you're not at work?

No, not really. I mean... I can't think of anything I do over and over like that. When I'm at home, I just sort of relax, so I don't think I have any specific routines or behaviors that I repeat. I haven't really noticed anything like that.
Do you ever have unwanted thoughts or ideas that keep repeating in your mind?
No, I don't think so. I don't really get stuck on specific thoughts like that. My mind wanders a lot, but it's not like the same unwanted idea is playing on a loop or anything.
Do you think getting up from your desk helps you avoid doing something you don't want to do?

Yeah, probably. I mean, at work, if I see a claim file that needs a really long written explanation or a bunch of dense policy language checked, I definitely avoid it. I'll just... put it off and do all the easier, quick tasks instead. I'll keep doing that until I'm basically out of time. So getting up and walking away from my desk is probably just another way of putting off those heavier files.
Do you think you get up from your desk specifically to avoid tasks that you find difficult or unpleasant?

Yeah, exactly. Like I was just saying... if a task is difficult or just really tedious, getting up is definitely a way to escape it for a bit. I don't always consciously think, "I'm going to walk away to avoid this," but... yeah, that's definitely what's happening.
Do you think getting up from your desk is usually in response to a specific task or type of task that you're trying to avoid?

Yeah, I think so. It's usually those complicated claim files I mentioned. The ones where I have to write a long explanation or read through a ton of dense policy language. If it's a quick, easy task, I'll just do it. But if it's one of those heavy ones, that's usually when I find myself suddenly needing to get up and walk around.
Do you feel like you're getting up from your desk to do something specific, like a ritual or a habit?

No, not really. It's not like I have to touch the doorframe three times or anything like that. It's really just... I need a break from staring at whatever complicated thing is on my screen. So I just get up to grab coffee or use the bathroom or just stretch my legs. It's not a specific routine, just a way to get away from the work for a minute.
Do you feel anxious or apprehensive when you think about returning to the task you avoided by getting up from your desk?

Not really anxious, no. It's more just... a feeling of dread, I guess? Like, I just really don't want to do it because I know it's going to be a slog. But I don't feel nervous or panicky about going back to my desk. I just know it's going to take a lot of mental energy that I don't really have at the moment.
Do you think getting up from your desk helps you avoid feeling overwhelmed or stressed?

Yeah, I guess you could say that. It's like... if I sit there staring at a massive file for too long, my brain just kind of hits a wall. So getting up definitely relieves that pressure for a second. It doesn't necessarily make the work any easier when I sit back down, but it stops me from just sitting there feeling completely stuck.
Do you think getting up from your desk is a way for you to escape feeling unhappy or uncomfortable?

I wouldn't say it's about feeling unhappy. Uncomfortable, maybe, but just in the sense that trying to focus on something tedious when my brain won't cooperate is frustrating. I'm not getting up because I'm sad or trying to escape some deep emotional thing. I just... I just need to step away from the paperwork for a minute because my focus is shot.
Has your behavior of getting up from your desk affected your relationships with your coworkers or supervisor?

Yeah, definitely with my supervisor. Actually, he just put me on performance coaching recently. My claim files are falling behind, and... well, my accuracy is being questioned now, too. It's a real problem because I've been aiming for the senior adjuster track, and I'm really worried I could lose that opportunity if things keep going like this.
Has getting up from your desk and avoiding tasks affected anything outside of your job?

Not really. I mean, outside of work, I don't have a desk I'm supposed to be glued to for eight hours. If I'm at home and I get up to walk around or switch what I'm doing, it doesn't really matter. So, no, I haven't noticed it causing any problems with my friends or personal life. It's pretty much just an issue at the office because that's where I'm expected to sit still and actually get through all those claims.
Do you think getting up from your desk is a way for you to avoid feeling overwhelmed by your emotions?

No, I don't think so. It's kind of like what I mentioned a minute ago—it's not really an emotional thing for me. I don't feel overwhelmed by feelings or anything like that. 

It's honestly just the work itself. When I can't focus on a claim, my brain just sort of hits a wall, and getting up is just a way to break that up. So, yeah, it doesn't really have anything to do with my emotions.
